output.answer_markdown: Williams expects to have sufficient liquidity to manage its businesses in 2022, based on forecasted cash flow from operations and other sources of liquidity [1]. Its listed sources include cash and cash equivalents on hand [4], and for its long-term debt maturities the potential sources are cash generated from operations, refinancing at attractive long-term rates or from the credit facility, and asset monetizations [2]. A later passage adds cash on hand to the maturity sources and notes that it retired $1.25 billion of notes in January 2022 with cash on hand [3].

provenance.quote: Based on our forecasted levels of cash flow from operations and other sources of liquidity, we expect to have sufficient liquidity to manage our businesses in 2022.

claims.text: Williams expects to have sufficient liquidity to manage its businesses in 2022, based on forecasted cash flow from operations and other sources of liquidity.

provenance.quote: Our potential sources of liquidity available to address these maturities include cash generated from operations, proceeds from refinancing at attractive long-term rates or from our credit facility, as well as proceeds from asset monetizations.
